newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SCHIPHOL AIRPORT ON TARGET 7 PCT FREIGHT GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: SCHIPHOL AIRPORT ON TARGET 7 PCT FREIGHT GROWTH.

text.p: The Dutch national airport is on target to handle roughly seven pct more airfreight this year, the director of cargo at Amsterdam's Schiphol airport told Reuters in an interview.

Frits Bisschop said the airport has moved from third to second place in airfreight terms when measured against its leading European competitors of London Heathrow, Paris Charles de Gaulle and Frankfurt.

Earlier this week, the airport announced that last year it handled 1,081,000 tonnes of air freight against 977,000 tonnes for 1995. Bisschop said the 1996 total would have been higher but for restrictions the airport imposed on noisy, older Chapter 2 aircraft.

"The measures we have taken to restrict the activities of airlines flying older and noisier aircraft have restricted growth. A lot of charter companies that had been operating Ilyushin, Boeing 707 and DC 8 aircraft no longer operate from Schiphol," he said.

In November 95, Schiphol imposed a surcharge on operators of Chapter 2 aircraft. In April 96 it banned take-offs of Chapter 2 aircraft between the hours of 2300 and 0600 and imposed an increased surcharge. In November it extended its restriction, banning take-offs and landings between 2300 and 0600 and further increased its surcharge.

The reduction of Boeing 707 and DC 8 aircraft was more than 50 percent last year but this was more than compensated for by other planes as the airport's freight traffic rose an overall 10.6 percent, Bisschop said.
Schiphol had had close to 3000 Chapter 2 freighters in 1995, and a total of 1400 in 1996.
"This year, 1997, that number will fall to just a few hundred," he stated.
